A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Weibo misinformation and social-bot dataset and study. All 17 pages of v1 and 23 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: V1 reports original misinformation-detection experiments, annotation-agreement measurements, and analyses of bot participation, content, sentiment, and stance.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds a human audit of automatic annotations, detailed expert evaluations, quantitative cluster analyses, and bot–polarization correlations.

M1.justification: The reported topic-clustering procedure changes from DBSCAN in v1 to largest-gap similarity thresholds and strongly connected groups in a directed graph in v2 Appendix C.1. The central calibrated expert ensemble, 0.75 bot threshold, and multimodal misinformation detector remain essentially the same.

E1.justification: Both versions study Chinese Weibo information from April 2018 through April 2024, retaining 11,393 misinformation items and 16,416 real-information items. EWECT and the Zhao et al. stance dataset are retained; v2's shortened STANCE name does not establish different coverage. Revised account counts and additional analyses concern the existing population.

E2.justification: V2 Table 7 adds an explicit comparison against an unfiltered 'All Expert' ensemble and reports the already-described 0.75-threshold annotator alongside the default annotator. The misinformation detector's complete comparator set is retained in v2 Table 6, despite the shorter main-text Table 2.

E3.justification: The annotation split changes from 8:2 to 8:1:1, and the stated expert learning rate changes from 10^-3 to 10^-4. Topic-constrained cross-validation now references the different clustering procedure. New evaluation protocols include a human audit of 50 predicted bots and 50 predicted humans, plus cluster comparisons using ROUGE-L with ten sampled items per cluster. These reported changes do not establish which earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds quantitative checks of within-topic versus between-topic similarity using silhouette scores and semantic/token heatmaps, bot–polarization correlation analyses, direct human validation of automatic labels, and expert-selection/threshold comparisons. The original modality ablations and sentiment analyses remain, with several moved to appendices.

E5.justification: V2 adds Cohen's kappa for human–machine agreement and Pearson estimates for count- and ratio-based associations. Ten-fold means and standard deviations, paired t-tests, and human-annotator Fleiss' kappa reporting are retained. No increased repeated-run count or new confidence-interval reporting is documented.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises bot/human counts from 68,040/411,635 to 65,749/345,886. Vanilla accuracy/F1 changes from 94.7/91.4 to 95.2/92.3, with numerous revised ablation scores; annotator accuracy changes from 83.96 to 85.03. These are revised results under changed reported settings, not established same-setting gains. New results include human–machine kappa 0.74, silhouette 0.29, and cluster-similarity and polarization-correlation measurements.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds formal definitions for the largest-gap clustering threshold and semantic/token pairwise cluster scores. Most other added formulas explain existing encoding, calibration, and similarity operations; the sentiment-variation definition is retained. Neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The dataset, automatic annotation, and bot–misinformation interplay contributions remain. V2 adds an explicit Weibo-specific first-study claim and foregrounds dataset distinguishability and annotation quality. Claims about creating echo chambers and reversing public stances are narrowed to providing a basis for echo chambers and generating similar content aimed at influencing opinions.

C2.justification: V2 adds rationales for excluding inactive accounts and trusting collection sources, qualifies echo-chamber membership as potential, and interprets new correlations as possible bot influence. The main limitations remain unchanged. Appendix B.5 introduces a precision-improvement interpretation that conflicts with Table 7: filtered-annotator precision is 83.3%, versus 89.5% for 'All Expert'.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands reproducibility information: source-account identities and query instructions, illustrated annotation guidelines, annotator payments and costs, feature normalization, frozen-encoder details, checkpoint links, and calibration-search settings. It also adds a dataset repository link and states that MISBOT has been published; external availability was not checked.

R1.justification: V2 substantially prunes literature coverage across misinformation detection, bot detection, and online safety, including the discussion of detector evasion and graph vulnerabilities. It adds Sayyadiharikandeh et al. (2020) to motivate specialized-expert ensembles and makes the Weibo-specific priority claim explicit. The central positioning around an understudied bot–misinformation interplay remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten; the dataset is named MISBOT and terminology shifts from news articles toward user posts. Dataset construction becomes numbered subsections with explicit annotation phases, while experimental descriptions and analyses are reorganized across the main text and expanded appendices.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figure 1, adds dataset/source examples, illustrated annotation guidelines, expert and source tables, and cluster heatmaps. Several existing figures move to appendices, the clustering visualization gains a silhouette annotation, and the full ablation table is retained in the appendix alongside a shortened main-text display.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, expanded collection and implementation documentation, a separate annotation test split, and a 100-account human audit make the dataset easier to reproduce and assess. Quantitative cluster checks and more qualified echo-chamber claims strengthen the paper. The net gain is limited by remaining observational overinterpretation and the new expert-filtering precision claim contradicted by Table 7.
